focus: /ʃ/ (sugar, delicious) vs /tʃ/ (chicken, kitchen) · schwa in 'a lot of' /ə lɒt əv/ · weak 'of' /əv/ · 'a few / a little' rhythm · /ʒ/ (usually, measure)
focus_ar: /ʃ/ مقابل /tʃ/، والشوا في 'a lot of'، و 'of' الخفيفة، وإيقاع 'a few / a little'، و /ʒ/
arabic_challenge: Arabic has ش (/ʃ/) but no /tʃ/, so 'chicken' can become 'shicken'. Quantifier phrases like 'a lot of' and 'a little' are full of weak schwas that Arabic learners tend to pronounce as full vowels, making the phrase sound heavy.

isolation.instructions: /ʃ/ (sugar, sure, delicious) is a long continuous hiss — like Arabic ش. /tʃ/ (chicken, cheese, kitchen) STARTS with a /t/ stop, then bursts into /ʃ/. Feel the little stop at the start of /tʃ/.
isolation.instructions_ar: /ʃ/ صفير مستمر (زي ش). /tʃ/ يبدأ بوقفة /t/ وبعدها ينفجر لـ /ʃ/. حس بالوقفة الصغيرة في أول /tʃ/.

sentence_practice: I add sugar to fresh chicken.
I wash the dishes in the kitchen.
daily_drills.record_this: I add a little sugar to the fresh chicken. The cheese sandwich is delicious, and I always wash the dishes in the kitchen after lunch.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'shop' then 'chop'. Only the second should begin with a hard stop.

target_sounds: schwa in 'a lot of' /ə lɒt əv/

isolation.instructions: 'A lot of' is three weak-strong-weak beats: /ə lɒt əv/. Only 'lot' is stressed; 'a' and 'of' are tiny schwas. It flows as one quantifier chunk before a noun.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'a lot of' ثلاث نبرات: خفيف-قوي-خفيف /ə lɒt əv/. 'lot' بس منبورة، و 'a' و 'of' شوا صغيرة.
practice: a lot of sugar, a lot of people

sentence_practice: There is a lot of sugar in this.
We have a lot of food for the party.
It takes a lot of time.
daily_drills.record_this: There is a lot of sugar in this cake. We have a lot of food and a lot of drinks for the party, but it took a lot of time to cook.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'a lot of food' as one chunk. Is only 'lot' stressed, with tiny 'a' and 'of'?

isolation.instructions: 'Of' is almost never /ɒv/. It weakens to /əv/ or just /ə/: a cup of tea = 'cuppa tea', a piece of cake = 'piece-ə-cake'. Never stress it.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'of' نادرًا تكون /ɒv/. بتخف لـ /əv/ أو /ə/: a cup of tea → cuppa tea. ومش بتتنبر.

sentence_practice: I'd like a cup of tea and a piece of cake.
We need a kilo of rice and a bottle of oil.
daily_drills.record_this: I'd like a cup of tea and a piece of cake, please. We also need a kilo of rice and a bottle of oil, but there's plenty of time to shop.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'cup of tea' fast. Does 'of' shrink to /ə/, sounding like 'cuppa'?

isolation.instructions: 'A few' (countable) and 'a little' (uncountable) are quantifier chunks: a-FEW, a-LITTLE. 'A' is weak; the stress is on few/little. Use 'a few' with plurals, 'a little' with uncountables.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'a few' (معدود) و 'a little' (غير معدود) وحدات: a-FEW, a-LITTLE. 'a' خفيفة والنبر على few/little.

sentence_practice: I have a few friends and a little time.
Add a little salt and a few olives.
daily_drills.record_this: I have a few close friends and a little free time this week. For the recipe, add a little salt and a few olives, then wait a few minutes.
daily_drills.self_check: Are you using 'a few' with countables (friends) and 'a little' with uncountables (time, salt)?

isolation.instructions: /ʒ/ is the VOICED partner of /ʃ/ — a soft buzzing 'zh' as in 'usually', 'measure', 'television', 'decision'. Arabic has no /ʒ/ in standard form, so it often becomes /z/ or /dʒ/.
isolation.instructions_ar: /ʒ/ هو النسخة المجهورة من /ʃ/ — صوت 'ژ' ناعم زي 'usually'. العربية الفصحى مفيهاش /ʒ/ فبتتحول لـ /z/ أو /dʒ/.

sentence_practice: I usually watch television in the evening.
It was a pleasure to meet you.
daily_drills.record_this: I usually watch television in the evening for leisure. It was a real pleasure to meet you, and I think you made a good decision.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'usually'. Is the middle a soft buzzing /ʒ/, not a hard /dʒ/ (like 'j') or /z/?

challenge_sentences: There's a lot of sugar and a little salt.
I usually cook chicken with fresh cheese.
We need a few onions and a bottle of oil.
The fish and chips were delicious.
daily_drills.record_this: There's a lot of sugar and a little salt in this dish. I usually cook chicken with fresh cheese. We need a few onions and a bottle of oil. The fish and chips at that shop were delicious.
daily_drills.self_check: Check: /ʃ/ vs /tʃ/ (shop/chop), weak 'of', and 'a few' vs 'a little' with the right nouns.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself talking about food and cooking. Then listen back and check each feature.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك وانت تتكلم عن الأكل والطبخ، وبعدين اسمع وراجع كل نقطة.
test_yourself.passage: I usually cook at home because restaurant food has a lot of sugar and a lot of salt. My favourite dish is chicken with rice. First I wash the chicken, then I add a little oil, a few onions and some fresh spices. I don't use much sugar, just a little. For dessert I make a cheese cake — it's delicious. I usually drink a cup of tea after lunch. Cooking is a pleasure for me, and it's my favourite way to relax during my leisure time. On special occasions I make fish and chips for the whole family.

sounds_to_check./ʃ/ vs /tʃ/: wash, fresh, delicious, fish — chicken, cheese, cheesecake, chips
sounds_to_check.'a lot of' schwa: a lot of sugar, a lot of salt
sounds_to_check.weak 'of': cup of tea, way of relaxing
sounds_to_check.'a few / a little': a few onions, a little oil, a little sugar

scoring_guide.90_100: 'chicken' is never 'shicken', quantifier chunks flow with weak schwas. Ready for week 9.
scoring_guide.70_89: Good; occasional heavy 'of' or 'a lot of'.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, saying each quantifier phrase as one smooth chunk.

for_arabic_speakers: You have ش (/ʃ/); /tʃ/ is /t/ + /ʃ/ said together — build 'chicken' from that, not from ش.
Quantifier chunks ('a lot of', 'a little') are mostly weak schwas — only the middle word is stressed.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
